why: A (submanifold N ⊆ V, f = F|N, read in any T ≃ₜ N) computes H_*(N^a, N^{a'}) for a slab whose ends a' < a are REGULAR values, with any number of critical points on the one critical level inside (dimension = number of them of index i), builds the filtration by regular values, proves finiteness of H_*(N), plus the arithmetic exists_separating_seq and 'a global max is critical'. B (abstract compact M) takes any a_0 < … < a_k with M^{a_0} = ∅, M^{a_k} = M and {critical, f ≤ a_i} = {p_0..p_{i-1}}, which forces distinct critical values but allows a_i to BE a critical value f(p_{i-1}). A ⇒ B fails genuinely on that case: it needs H_*(M^{c+δ}, M^c) = 0 at a critical level (Remark 3.4 on a manifold), which the project proves only on a vector space (isStrongDeformationRetract_sublevel_crit), and A's slab lemmas exclude critical ends. For regular ends A ⇒ B would follow by Whitney transport and sublevel_step. B ⇒ A fails: B is vacuous when two critical points share a level (A is not), and B asserts no existence of a filtration and no finiteness.
B_issue: MorseFilt does not require the a_i to be regular values (Milnor's intent, since his proof uses Theorems 3.1/3.2 on [a_{i-1}, a_i]); the claim stays true but is then stronger than Milnor's argument gives.
